Looking at this logic puzzle, I need to work systematically through the statements to determine the truth values for Vernell, Sherrie, and Fletcher.

## Starting with Known Facts

**Yoland tells the truth** (given directly).

From statement 7: Delbert says Yoland tells the truth. Since Yoland does tell the truth, **Delbert tells the truth**.

## Building a Chain of Deductions

**Ka tells the truth:**

- From statements 10 & 38: Mateo and Orly contradict each other, so exactly one tells the truth
- Since Delbert tells the truth, exactly one more from {Orly, Mateo} tells the truth = 2 total ✓

**Conception lies:**
- From statement 27: Conception says exactly one of {Ka, Miguel, Ollie} tells the truth
- From statements 13 & 29: Miguel and Ollie contradict each other, so exactly one tells the truth
- Ka tells the truth, so that's 2 people total, making Conception's statement false

**Audrie tells the truth:**

- From statements 34 & 40: Orlando and Mavis contradict each other, so exactly one tells the truth
- Conception lies, so exactly 1 of the three tells the truth ✓

**Shalonda tells the truth:**

- Audrie tells the truth, so exactly 1 of the three tells the truth ✓

**Sima lies:**

- Shalonda tells the truth; if Melissa and Martha both tell the truth, all 3 tell the truth (not matching the statement)
- If both lie, only 1 tells the truth (not matching the statement) ✗

Continuing this chain: **Rashida lies, Jaymie lies, Jim lies, Sherrie lies, Kandi lies, Ryan tells the truth, Christie lies, Raymond lies**.

**Willian tells the truth:**

- Raymond lies; whether Madeleine/Owen both tell the truth (giving 2) or both lie (giving 0), the statement is true

**Alexis lies:**

- Willian tells the truth, so Alexis lies

**Alejandro lies:**
- From statement 2 and statements 28 & 46: Exactly one of {Oliver, Marvin} tells the truth
- For exactly 2 of {Alexis, Oliver, Marvin} to tell the truth, Alexis must tell the truth
- But Alexis lies, so Alejandro's statement is false

**Antwan lies:**
- From statement 39: Antwan says exactly 2 of {Alejandro, Olga, Ozzie} tell the truth
- From statements 3 & 12: At most one of {Olga, Ozzie} tells the truth
- Alejandro lies, so at most 1 of all three tells the truth ✗

## Finding the Three Answers

**Vernell lies:**
- From statement 30: Vernell says all 3 or only 1 of {Sherrie, Maynard, Marina} tells the truth
- From statements 18 & 48: Maynard and Marina have the same truth value
- Sherrie lies; whether Maynard/Marina both tell the truth (giving 2) or both lie (giving 0), neither matches the statement

**Sherrie lies:** (already established above)

**Fletcher lies:**

- From statements 33 & 47: Morgan and Olympia have opposite truth values (exactly one lies)
- Antwan lies, so two of the three lie, contradicting Fletcher's statement
